_doc: The men's needs, the camp and the fire (docs/survival.md, #65, #68; src/smyana/survival.lobster). Needs run from 100 (fine) to 0 (spent), per man. Rates are a game hour's worth (the clock: route.json's day_minutes, a night faster). start_food: portions each man leaves the village with, one a man a day.

fed._doc: Hunger. 'per_hour' is how much a man awake loses an hour, more by 'work' hundredths while he fells or digs and 'loaded' while he carries; 'asleep' asleep. A hot meal at a lit fire fills him, a cold one gives 'cold_meal'. At 0 he loses 'starving_hp' health an hour.

warm._doc: Warmth goes toward the air's: 'air' by season (summer, autumn, winter, spring; between them by the year), less 'altitude' a hundred of the leg's altitude, 'night' at night, up to 'wind', 'rain' and 'snow' at their hardest, and 'wading' in a ford times how cold the water is (0..1). It falls 'fall' an hour toward it and rises 'rise'; within 'fire_tiles' of a lit fire the air is 'fire' warmer and it rises 'fire_rise'; asleep in a camp with others, 'huddle' warmer. At 0 he loses 'freezing_hp' health an hour.

rested._doc: Tiredness: 'per_hour' awake, 'loaded' hundredths of that while he walks loaded; 'asleep' back an hour in a camp. A man who is fed, warm and asleep heals 'heal_hp' an hour.

pace._doc: Below 'low' a need takes up to 'most' hundredths off a man's pace, each need its own share.

camp._doc: Making camp (C): the men stand round the fire, the nearest 'ring_tiles' from it, and lay a fire: it costs 'wood' off their backs and takes 'lay_s' seconds, or 'lay_bare_s' if none of them carries wood, while two of them go off for dead wood (50 until 2026-11-13: Dominic, playing, "telling them to make camp, i got no fire"; the fireplace now shows while it is laid). A man within 'in_tiles' of it is in the camp; at night he sleeps there. The camp is struck when no man has been within 'in_tiles' for 'struck_s'. Woken by a shot, a man stays up 'woken_s'. The meal is at the first camp after 'meal_hour'.

fire_seen._doc: A lit fire draws the threats (docs/survival.md): seen at night 'night_tiles' off, through any cover; its smoke by day 'day_tiles'; wolves keep 'wolves_keep_tiles' off it; the bear smells a camp's food 'bear_smell_tiles' off.

forage._doc: What the wood gives, by its kind (the map's 'wood') and the season (docs/survival.md, #66; docs/gathering.md). Since 2026-11-13 (Dominic, playing: "gameplay is moving my mouse over everything to find something"; the gathering proposal he agreed: fewer, bigger finds you see, the men calling them out) a find is a STAND: 'stands' of them a place (from, to, by the run's seed), each holding 'amount' (from, to) of what it 'gives', food portions for the road or goods to take home. 'where' is where it grows: 'light' at the side paths' clearings and open glades (wild pears, dog rose and the berries fruit in the light, in deep shade the rose fails to fruit: Wikipedia, Rosa canina; the wild pear needs a lot of light, Pyrus pyraster), 'shade' deep under the old trees, eight tiles or more from the trail (ceps grow under spruce, fir, beech and oak, singly or two or three together: Wikipedia, Boletus edulis), 'high' on open stony ground (mountain tea, Sideritis scardica, grows above 1,500 m in the Rhodopes above Trigrad and is picked by hand in flower in July and August). A man at a stand gathers one a 'gather_s' seconds into his pack, up to 'most_men' men at once; right-click it with men chosen. 'call' is what the first man to come within 'call_tiles' of it says, once. What is taken stays taken.

winter.call: Rose hips, still on the bush.
Rose hips, still on the bush.

packs._doc: A man's pack (docs/survival.md, #67, #69): it holds 'most' of food portions and goods together; a bundle of wood on top weighs 'wood'. A full pack takes 'slow' hundredths off his pace (in proportion as it fills). X: the chosen men drop their packs where they stand, keeping 'keep_food' portions each; a pile left at the foot of an old tree is a cache. A pile is found by a patrol passing that sees it (the cover over it hides it as it hides a man: the leaves falling, the tree felled) and taken; the bear smells food in one from 'bear_smell_tiles' and eats it. Right-click a pile with men chosen and they share it out into their packs.

knowledge._doc: What the men learn (docs/survival.md, #70): the Roman drain at the ruins. Right-click the old road (its drain runs beside it) with men chosen and they stand at it and study; it takes 'man_hours' of men's time on the clock (four men about six hours; more men, quicker), and a man must give at least 'least_hours' of it to have learned it. Kept between the two visits to the ruins. Lost if every man who learned it dies.

finds._doc: What lies off the trail by the run's seed (docs/off-the-path.md, Dominic 2026-11-13: 'The goal is getting bak home with enough resources, knowledge and men to improve your village'): up to 'per_place' finds a place, no two of a kind, each at the end of a side path whose clearing has no game at it, the kind picked by 'weight' among those the place's wood has ('woods'; none: any). A 'hut' is a shepherds' hut, empty after the flocks go down in late October (the Sarakatsani leave the mountains on St Demetrius' day, 26 October): dry-stacked stone, a slab roof, one door, a hearth in the middle (summer-pasture huts of the Balkan mountains, parksdinarides.org). A camp made at it has its fire inside, seen only 'seen_tiles' off, and the men asleep in it are 'warm' warmer, out of the wind. A 'cache' is food and goods another band put by under stones ('food' and 'goods': from, to), found only by going down the path. 'honey' is wild bees in a hollow old tree (a Rhodope village's legend of oaks and walnuts whose hollows wild bees lived in, BNR 2023; swarms settled in hollow trees, BNR on Bulgarian beekeeping): 'food' portions, and the bear smells it as it smells a cache. A cache and the honey are taken like a pile of packs; a patrol that sees one takes it.

wares._doc: The goods the men take home, each a kind (docs/gathering.md; the gathering proposal Dominic agreed 2026-11-13: food for the road, and things for home that make the village better). 'herbs' are gathered at a stand of herbs or mountain tea (Sideritis scardica, the Rhodopes' mountain tea, drunk against coughs and colds); 'wax' is the comb of wild bees' honey, for candles; 'hides' are taken from a deer or boar the men kill; 'wool' is what another band left in its cache. Each is one place in a pack. 'line' is the tally's line at home, % the count ('one' when there is one).
